title: Same average, different ride
hook: Two games both pay +$1 a play on average. Is it safe to pick either one?

knows: the average (expected) payoff of a simple bet
doesNotKnow: spread (variance) as separate from the average
the risk of ending behind over a finite number of plays

misconception: Two games with the same average payoff are equally good, or equally safe, to play.
objective: The learner can explain that two games with the same average can leave very different shares of players behind, because a game paid through rare big wins has a wider spread of outcomes.

claims.text: Game X (win $10 or lose $8 on a coin flip) and Game Y (10% to win $55, else lose $5) both average +$1 per play.
claims.source: EV(X) = 0.5 x 10 - 0.5 x 8 = 1; EV(Y) = 0.1 x 55 - 0.9 x 5 = 1 (ev() in src/demos/probability/same-average-different-ride/model.ts).

claims.text: After 100 plays, Game X leaves a player behind (below $0) with chance 14%, Game Y with chance 32%.
claims.source: X ends 18W - 800, below 0 iff wins W <= 44: P(Bin(100, 0.5) <= 44) = 0.1356. Y ends 60W - 500, below 0 iff W <= 8: P(Bin(100, 0.1) <= 8) = 0.3209. exactBehind() in model.ts.

claims.text: Both games' average ending after 100 plays is +$100.
In a Game Y player's 100 plays, fewer than 9 wins means ending behind.
In the stage's 1,000 simulated players per game, 15% of X players and 32% of Y players ended behind; average endings were +$94 and +$105.
claims.source: crowd() in model.ts, seed 77 (untuned: the first seed tried). Over 300 other seeds the X count ranged 109-166 of 1,000 (median 135) and Y 273-365 (median 321).

claims.text: The 20 lines are seeded players; the first batch has 1 of 20 behind for X and 5 of 20 for Y.
claims.source: players() in model.ts, seed 4242, untuned. Batches 1-3 show 1, 2, 3 behind for X and 8, 6, 11 for Y: a batch of 20 is noisy, which is why the stage also counts 1,000.

recall.question: Two investments both average +5% a year. One moves a little each year; the other is usually slightly down but sometimes soars. Over five years, which more often leaves you below where you started?
recall.why: Same average, different spread. When the average is carried by rare big wins, most individual paths miss them and end behind.
